title: Downhill running increases markers of muscle damage and impairs the maximal voluntary force production as well as the late phase of the rate of voluntary force development
claims: Ten recreational runners performed a 30-min downhill run at 10 km/h on a -20% (-11.3 degree) motorized treadmill.

Knee extensor maximal voluntary isometric force (MVIC) showed moderate decrements that recovered after 4 days; serum CK, quadriceps swelling and soreness increased and were fully resolved after 4 days in this sample.
The late (100-200 ms) phase of rate of voluntary force development was impaired and recovered after 3-4 days, while the early (0-50 ms) phase was not impaired.
The sample was small, recreational and male; the 4-day timeline is a treadmill lab result and does not set a universal recovery deadline for trail running.
